item.title: Minor--Skein Spatial Negami Splitting Vectors and a Gluing Formula for Marked State Sums
item.description: arXiv:2611.31289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We organize the edge states of a decorated spatial graph by the minors of their underlying abstract graphs. For pieces with disjoint edge sets, Negami's component formula and functorial ribbon evaluation express each marked sector as a boundary pairing, provided the local data determine its marker. We give two explicit rules for this last step. A two-terminal rule for $3$-connected targets tests each piece with and without a virtual edge. At arbitrary finite vertex boundaries, records of partial branch sets determine the occurrence of each fixed simple target. The rules assign a weight once per edge state, even when the state contains several minor models.
item.dc:creator: Iwao Mizukai

item.title: Ramsey numbers of fixed-length cycles, paths and stars in set-colored triple systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.31290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R_3(H;r,s,t)$ be the least order of a complete triple system in which every assignment of $s$ of $r$ colors to each triple forces a copy of $H$ whose edges share at least $t$ colors. Fix $r\ge s\ge t\ge1$ and let $n$ count edges. We prove that the Ramsey numbers of the linear path and the linear cycle of fixed length $n$ are both $\gamma n+o(n)$ as $n\to\infty$, with $\gamma=2$ if and only if $r=s$. For tight paths the corresponding formula is $\tau n+o(n)$, with the same coefficient for tight cycles when $3\mid n$. To obtain exactly $n$ edges in a linear cycle, we choose the parity of the connections and vary the lengths of the paths they join. For a linear star $S_n$, whose edges meet only at the center, $R_3(S_n;r,s,t)=cn+O(n^{2/3})$ for fixed colors. For fixed $n\ge2$ and $s,t$ as $r\to\infty$, it is asymptotic to $\sqrt{6a_n\binom{r}{t}/\binom{s}{t}}$, where $a_n=n(n-1)$ for odd $n$ and $a_n=n(2n-3)/2$ for even $n$. For a tight star, whose edges share a pair, the leading term is $(n-1)\binom{r}{t}/\binom{s}{t}$ in both regimes. For a fixed linear path of $n\ge3$ edges and fixed $s\ge t\ge2$, the upper bound is $(2000h/1307+o(1))\binom{r}{t}/\binom{s}{t}$ as $r\to\infty$, where $h=\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$.
item.dc:creator: Xuanyu Cao, Chunxiang Wang

item.title: Power-Law Lower Bounds for Edges in Odd Induced Subgraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.31300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite simple graph $G$, let $g(G)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an induced subgraph of $G$ in which every vertex has odd degree. Motivated by Scott's question of whether $g(G) \geq cm$ for every graph with $m$ edges, we prove that $g(G) \geq cm^{4/7}$ for every finite simple graph with $m \geq 1$ edges, where $c > 0$ is an absolute constant. For bipartite graphs, we obtain the stronger bound $g(B) \geq cm^{2/3}$.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyu Liu

item.title: Bounds for the small Davenport constant of extraspecial groups of exponent three
item.description: arXiv:2611.31324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E_s$ be the extraspecial group of order $3^{2s+1}$ and exponent three. We prove $4s+2r+2\le d(E_s\times C_3^r)\le 4s+2r+3$ for $s\ge1$ and $r\ge0$. For $s\ge2$, the degree in the polynomial proof is optimal among weights depending only on group-element multiplicities modulo three. For $s=2$, we reduce the question in all ranks to an abelian subset-sum problem with a fixed set of forbidden values in a $77$-dimensional space. We show that this set, together with zero, contains no $76$-dimensional subspace. The equality $d(E_2\times C_3^r)=2r+10$ in all ranks is not established here.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Volkmann

item.title: Quadratic periods after adjoining one move to a fixed subtraction game
item.description: arXiv:2611.31336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zhang conjectured that adjoining one move $c$ to a fixed subtraction set $S$ gives a Grundy sequence whose least preperiod and period are both $O_S(c)$. For every $q=20+9s$ with $s\ge0$, take $S=\{3,6,q-3\}$. Along $c=qk+1$ with $k\ge2$, the Grundy and win/loss sequences are periodic from heap zero with common least period $(k+2)(c+6)-11$, asymptotic to $c^2/q$. For $\{3,6,17\}$ we determine both least periods and preperiods for every positive $c$ and verify the complete table in Lean. Fixed bases with the same entire Grundy sequence realize infinitely many distinct positive quadratic coefficients for the augmented period. A second fixed triple gives a quadratic Grundy preperiod while the win/loss sequence repeats from heap zero. A third has a quadratic Grundy period but only a linear win/loss period. For an arbitrary fixed $S$, a linear bound on both Grundy invariants implies eventual affine formulas with integer coefficients on residue classes. The same finite-state method extends four numerical tables of Zhang. We also give the entire augmented sequence for $c>\max S$ when the losing heaps of $S$ are exactly the multiples of a fixed integer.
item.dc:creator: Yuwen Pan

item.title: RSK with a twist, mirabolic Steinberg variety, and Pak--Postnikov representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.31409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There is a beautiful interplay between the classical Robinson--Schensted correspondence and the Steinberg variety, which is the union of conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V)$. The irreducible components of the Steinberg variety gives the geometric interpretation of RS, and Pak--Postnikov description of RS as U,D operators is the combinatorics shadow of the $S_n\times S_n$-representation inside the top homology of the Steinberg variety. We study the conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V) \times L(\lambda)$, where $L(\lambda)$ is an irreducible representation of $GL(V)$. We show that there are only three families of $L(\lambda)$ such that $Fl(V)\times Fl(V) \times L(\lambda)$ has finitely many orbits. These families are determinant twists of classical RS, Travkin's mirabolic RSK and its Fourier dual. We extend the combinatorial interpretation of RS in terms of U,D operators to mirabolic RSK. Finally, we give a filtration of the top homology of the mirabolic Steinberg variety in which each graded piece is a Pak--Postnikov $S_n \times S_n$-representations.
item.dc:creator: Son Nguyen

item.title: Cycle popping and positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.31443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every monomial in the cluster variables of a linear Laurent phenomenon algebra is a nonnegative combination of cluster monomials, as conjectured by Lam and the second author. The proof uses Wilson's cycle popping. We also give a new proof of Laurent positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras, previously established by the first author.
item.dc:creator: Ross Glew, Pavlo Pylyavskyy

item.title: Major progress on hamiltonian saturation in hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.31599v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $1\leq \ell< k$, an \emph{$\ell$-overlapping $k$-cycle} is a $k$-uniform hypergraph in which, for some cyclic vertex ordering, every edge consists of $k$ consecutive vertices and every two consecutive edges share exactly $\ell$ vertices. A $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ is $\ell$-\emph{hamiltonian saturated} if $H$ does not contain an $\ell$-overlapping Hamilton $k$-cycle but every hypergraph obtained from $H$ by adding a new edge does contain such a cycle. For $n$ divisible by $k-\ell$, let sat$(n,k,\ell)$ be the smallest number of edges in an $\ell$-hamiltonian saturated $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. In the case of graphs Clark and Entringer showed in 1983 that, for sufficiently large $n$, sat$(n,2,1)=\lceil \frac{3n}2\rceil$. By ad hoc methods, the present authors proved previously that sat$(n,k,\ell)=\Theta(n^{\ell})$ for some rather narrow and scattered ranges of $\ell$. In this paper we present a unified proof of this equality for all $k$ and $\ell>k/2$.
item.dc:creator: Andrzej \.Zak, Andrzej Ruci\'nski

item.title: Normal edge-transitive bi-Cayley graphs of prime valency over nonabelian simple groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.31759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a connected graph of prime valency admitting a nonabelian simple group $R$ that acts semiregularly on the vertices with exactly two orbits. We prove that if the normalizer of $R$ in $Aut(\Gamma)$ is edge-transitive, then $\Gamma$ is bipartite and $R$ is characteristic in $Aut(\Gamma)$. We derive consequences for Cayley graphs and a criterion for semisymmetry. As an application, we construct bi-Cayley graphs over $A_p$ from the conjugates of a $3$-cycle under a cyclic group of order $p$, where $p>5$ is prime. These graphs are semisymmetric precisely when the support of the $3$-cycle is not a three-term arithmetic progression in $\mathbb{F}_p$.
item.dc:creator: Zai Ping Lu, Hai Ze Wang

item.title: A logarithmic saving in the sum-free subset problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.31828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every sufficiently large $n$ there is a set of $n$ positive integers, all at most $n^2$, whose largest sum-free subset has size at most $n/3+O(n/\log n)$. We bound the number of small divisible elements in a dense set with few Schur triples. A fixed-accuracy cyclic model gives a rotation, and the original integer triple count controls its density at the required scale.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolu Zhang

item.title: Modular Schur functions and Macdonald characters
item.description: arXiv:2611.31879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modular Schur functions arose from the problem of determining the characters of simple polynomial representations of the general linear group in positive characteristic. We prove three results about these functions. (i) In finitely many variables, we obtain two bases for a space of symmetric polynomials with bounded degree in each variable, one consisting of modular Schur polynomials and the other of products of truncated complete symmetric polynomials. (ii) We determine the signs of the nonzero Schur coefficients of modular Schur functions, show that their absolute values are at most the factorial of the block weight, and characterize equality. (iii) Over an infinite field of prime characteristic, a modular Schur polynomial is a simple polynomial character exactly when its indexing partition satisfies the Carter condition, provided the number of variables is at least the degree. Thus we prove three conjectures formulated by Walker (1994). We also use the Heisenberg operators from the Schur coefficient calculation to prove positivity for Macdonald characters. After centering the Macdonald parameters at one and negating the auxiliary variables, the normalized power-sum matrix entries of the Macdonald creation operator have nonnegative integer coefficients, which yields nonnegative rational coefficients for normalized Macdonald characters. The result for the creation operator confirms a conjecture of Ben Dali and D'Adderio (2024).
item.dc:creator: Naihuan JIng, Ning Liu

item.title: Blow-up size for the noncommutative rank of linear symbolic matrices with low-rank coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.31963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The noncommutative rank (nc-rank) of a linear symbolic matrix $A = A_0 x_0 + A_1 x_1 + \dots + A_m x_m$ is the supremum of $1/k$ times the rank of the $k$-th blow-up $\sum_i A_i \otimes X_i$ of $A$, where $X_i$ are $k \times k$ matrices consisting of distinct variables. In this paper, we show that the blow-up size needed to attain the nc-rank is bounded by the ranks of the coefficient matrices. More precisely, if $A_1, \dots, A_m$ have rank at most $r$, with no restriction on $A_0$, then the $k$-th blow-up attains the nc-rank for every $k \geq r$. This holds for rectangular matrices over an arbitrary field, and unifies and extends the known results that $k = 1$ suffices for rank-one coefficients (Lov\'asz, 1989; Ivanyos, Karpinski, and Saxena, 2010) and that $k = 2$ suffices for skew-symmetric coefficients of rank two (Oki and Soma, 2025). We present two applications. First, if $r$ is a constant, then the nc-rank of an $n \times n$ linear symbolic matrix can be computed by a randomized algorithm with $O(m n^2 + n^\omega)$ arithmetic operations over a sufficiently large field, where $\omega$ is the matrix multiplication exponent. Second, the hierarchy of polytopes introduced by Hirai (2026), which converges to the nc-independent set polytope, stabilizes at the $r$-th level; this is based on a counterpart of our main result for the degree of the Dieudonn\'e determinant.
item.dc:creator: Yuni Iwamasa

item.title: Rich\'ard Wiegandt's theory of M\"obius products revisited
item.description: arXiv:2611.32124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a 1959 paper Rich\'ard Wiegandt defined a general notion of M\"obius product of functions on arbitrary locally finite posets, and determined when this product is commutative and associative. He gave an example showing that not all locally finite posets allow such a M\"obius product. Here we characterize those posets of height 3 that can be equipped with a commutative and associative M\"obius product.
item.dc:creator: P\'eter P. P\'alfy

item.title: The backtrackless circuits of $D(k,q)$ obtained by lifting
item.description: arXiv:2611.32201v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For integer $k\geq2$ and power $q$ of prime $p$, the algebraic bipartite graph $D(k,q)$, proposed by Lazebnik and Ustimenko in 1993, is $q$-regular, edge-transitive and of girth at least $k+4$. For $q\geq4$, it was conjectured in 1995 that the exact girth of $D(k,q)$, denoted by $g(D(k,q))$, is equal to $g_k$, where $g_k$ is defined as $k+5$ if $2\nmid k$ and as $k+4$ if $2|k$. It is now known that this conjecture is true when $g_k$ is of form $hp^t$, where $h$ is a factor of $4(q-1)$. Sun proved in her thesis (2017) that, for $n\not\equiv 1(\bmod\ 4)$, any backtrackless circuit (BC) of length $l$ in $D(n,q)$ can be lifted to BCs of length $pl$ in $D(k,q)$, where $k$ is $p(n+5)-5$ if $n\equiv 3(\bmod\ 4)$ and $p(n+4)-4$ otherwise. This result implies that, provided $g(D(n,q))=g_n$, we must have $g(D(k,q))=g_k$ for any $k$ in the set $\{p^sg_n-5|s\geq 0\}$ if $n\equiv 3(\bmod\ 4)$ and for any $k$ in the set $\{p^sg_n-5|s\geq 0\}\cup\{p^sg_n-4|s\geq 0\}$ otherwise, where $D(1,q)$ is defined as the graph $D(2,q)$ if any. Sun's proof for this result is simplified in this paper, with the help of some new automorphisms of the graph $D(k,q)$ that are combinations of the known ones. A new proof for this result is also given in the last section of this paper by using a class of homogeneous polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyan Cheng, Chen Zhang, Yuansheng Tang, Ming Xu

item.title: On the bounds of path-unique subgraph of De Bruijn graph
item.description: arXiv:2611.32249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The De Bruijn graph is a directed graph G(n, m) such that V = (Zn)m and there is an edge from A to B iff A deletes the first coordinate equals to B deletes the last coordinate. Based on the background of achieving DNA labeling with minimum labels, we consider the De Brujin graph and its path-unique subgraph with maximum edges. Hofmeister gave an estimation of the lower bound and upper bound of the biggest number of the ratio of the edges we can keep in a path-unique subgraph, given the upper bound and lower bound and proved that the limit goes to 1 when n tends to infinity, and a lower bound m+1 2m when m tends to infinity. In this article, we will give some better construction of path-unique subgraph then give a better estimation in each condition, and show that when n tends to infinity the graph is almost (m + 1)-partite
item.dc:creator: Jiacheng Cao, Xin Wei, Xiande Zhang

item.title: Weak oddness to resistance ratios in snarks
item.description: arXiv:2611.32276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. If $G$ is not 3-edge-colourable, we call it a \textit{snark}. The \textit{resistance} of $G$, denoted $r(G)$, is the minimum number of edges which can be removed from $G$ in order to render $G$ 3-edge-colourable. The \textit{oddness} of $G$, denoted $\omega(G)$, is the minimum number of odd components in any 2-factor of $G$. The \textit{weak oddness} of $G$, denoted $\omega'(G)$, is the minimum number of odd components in any even factor of $G$. In their comprehensive survey paper on measurements of uncolourability in cubic graphs, Fiol et al. conjectured the following two statements for a snark $G$: $\omega(G) \leq 2r(G)$ and $\omega'(G) \leq 2r(G)$ \cite{FiolMazzuoccoloSteffen2018}. Previously, we disproved the former by proving that the ratio of oddness to weak oddness, and hence the ratio of oddness to resistance, can in fact be arbitrarily large \cite{Allie2019}. In this paper, we prove a slightly stronger version of the latter: $\omega'(G) < 2r(G)$. The proof centres around substructures in $G$, given a minimal colouring $f$, which we call \textit{meta-Kempe chains}.
item.dc:creator: Imran Allie

item.title: The Orientable Genus of Generalized Corona Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.32318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The generalized corona of a graph with a family of graphs, one for each vertex, is obtained by joining every vertex of the base graph to all vertices of its own copy of the corresponding graph; the corona of Frucht and Harary is the case in which all graphs in the family are equal. Each attached copy meets the rest of the graph in a single vertex, so additivity of the orientable genus over blocks reduces the genus of a generalized corona to the genus of the base graph plus the genera of the graphs obtained from the attached graphs by adding a dominating vertex. We study this last quantity through faces that meet every vertex, and we determine it for complete graphs, balanced complete bipartite graphs, wheels, prisms, antiprisms, the Petersen graph (value 2). The Petersen case follows from a face-length criterion. We also obtain bounds under edge addition, a formula for iterated coronas, a criterion for two coronas taken in opposite order to have the same genus, and we show that the corona is not associative with respect to the genus.
item.dc:creator: Jyoti Anant Pulgam, Prashant Malavadkar

item.title: A Sylow reduction for isomorphisms of Cayley graphs on abelian groups of cube-free order
item.description: arXiv:2611.32366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The isomorphism problem for Cayley graphs is one of the fundamental problems in algebraic combinatorics. Dobson studied this isomorphism problem and asked whether, assuming that the group generated by the left regular representation and its conjugate under an isomorphism admits a complete sequence of normal block systems, the isomorphism problem for Cayley digraphs on a finite abelian group of cube-free order can be reduced to the corresponding problem on its Sylow subgroups. We answer this question affirmatively. We first prove that color-preserving isomorphisms preserving the fiber partition on direct products $A\times H$ of abelian groups of coprime orders, where $|H|$ is a prime or the square of a prime, have a product decomposition property. Applying this property successively to the Sylow subgroups of a cube-free-order abelian group $G$, we show that if two colored binary Cayley structures on $G$ are connected by a color-preserving isomorphism $f$ for which $\langle G_L,f^{-1}G_Lf\rangle$ admits a complete sequence of block systems, then they are also connected by a color-preserving Sylow coordinate isomorphism. This yields the corresponding Sylow reduction for solving sets.
item.dc:creator: Tingzeng Wu, Liang Qin, Yong Yu, Xing Gao

item.title: A proof of the toughness conjecture for Kneser graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.32376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As a measure of the connectivity of graphs, Chv\'atal \cite{Chvatal} introduced the concept of toughness. For integers $k\geq2$ and $n\geq2k+1$, the Kneser graph $\KG(n,k)$ has all the $k$-subsets of $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ as its vertices, and two vertices are adjacent if they are disjoint. Cioab\u{a} and Wong~\cite{CW} determined the toughness of $\KG(n,2)$. Park et al.~\cite{Park} determined the toughness of $\KG(n,k)$ when $k=3,4$ and $k\geq5$ for large $n$. They \cite{Park} proposed a conjecture for $k\geq5$ and other values of $n$. In this paper, we resolve this conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Guang Li, Wenqian Zhang

item.title: Three combinatorial identities of the Rogers-Ramanujan type
item.description: arXiv:2611.32425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The purpose of the present paper is to establish three combinatorial Rogers--Ramanujan type identities. Although their motivation comes from the representation theory of affine Lie algebra of type $A_2^{(2)}$, our proofs are entirely combinatorial and analytic. They follow the automata-theoretic approach introduced by Takigiku and Tsuchioka in their proof of Nandi's conjecture and adapt it to the present setting.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Capparelli, Arne Meurman, Mirko Primc

item.title: Homothetic Copies of Polytopes and Binomial Barcodes
item.description: arXiv:2611.32429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite full-dimensional configuration, and put $F_X(N)=\max_{S\subset\mathbb{R}^d, |S|=N}\#\{(\mathbf{v},\lambda)\in\mathbb{R}^d\times(0,\infty):\mathbf{v}+\lambda X\subseteq S\}$. Elekes and Erd\H{o}s posed the problem of estimating $F_X(N)$. In this article, we determine its exact value when $X$ is the vertex set of a simplex. For several other classes of configurations, we obtain sharp asymptotic bounds and exact extremal values. We also introduce binomial barcodes for order polytopes and a recursive criterion for their effectiveness. In particular, if $X$ is the vertex set of the three-dimensional cube, then, for $n\ge 1$, $F_X(n^3)=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}j^3=\left(\frac{n(n-1)}{2}\right)^2$.
item.dc:creator: Site Mou

item.title: Trace-defined double covers of the $S_3$-involution graph of $PSL_2(2^n)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.32436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $q=2^n\ge 4$, we construct a family of Deza double covers $\Gamma(q,\xi)$ of the $S_3$-involution graph of $PSL_2(q)$, parametrized by $\xi\in\mathbb F_q^*$. We show that each resulting cover is connected, arc-transitive and amply regular with parameters $(2(q^2-1),q,Tr(\xi),1)$, where $Tr$ denotes the absolute trace. We also show that the trace-one covers are antipodal of diameter $5$ and girth $3$, whereas the trace-zero covers are non-antipodal of diameter $3$ and girth $5$. For $q=4$, these cases yield the well-known icosidodecahedral and dodecadodecahedral graphs, respectively. Then we determine the distance distributions and full automorphism groups of the covers and prove that, for fixed $q$, two covers are isomorphic if and only if their defining parameters lie in the same Frobenius orbit. We also express the Ramanujan property of a cover in terms of the spectral norm of a signed adjacency matrix of the base graph.
item.dc:creator: G. A. Glinskikh, L. Yu. Tsiovkina

item.title: A sharp form of Welsh's log-concavity inequality for chromatic polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.32465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n\ge 1$, and let $P_G(x)$ be its chromatic polynomial. In the early 1970s, Welsh conjectured that $P_G(k)^2 \ge P_G(k-1)P_G(k+1)$ holds for any positive integer $k$. This conjecture was also independently proposed by Brenti in 1992, while in 1997, Seymour disproved it for $k=6$ by constructing an infinite family of graphs of sufficiently large order as counterexamples. In 2005, Dong, Koh and Teo conjectured that $P_G(x)^2 \ge P_G(x-1)P_G(x+1)$ holds for all real $x\ge n$. In this paper, we prove that the inequality holds for all real $x\ge n-1$. Equality holds if and only if $n\ge 2$, $G$ is complete, and $x=n-1$. Moreover, the bound $x\ge n-1$ is best possible for every $n\ge 2$.
item.dc:creator: Meiqiao Zhang, Fengming Dong

item.title: Perfect state transfer in Grover walks on generalized Bethe trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.32469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We completely classify the generalized Bethe trees $B(d_0,d_1,\ldots,d_{n-1})$ that exhibit perfect state transfer between vertex states in Grover walks. We prove that such a tree exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if it is a path or a uniform subdivision of either $B(2,3)$ or $B(1,2,3)$. We also determine all transferring pairs and the minimum transfer times.
item.dc:creator: Koushik Bhakta, Bikash Bhattacharjya

item.title: A Proof of the Balister-Gy\H{o}ri-Schelp Conjecture on Perfect Matchings with Prescribed Differences
item.description: arXiv:2611.32557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the conjecture of Balister, Gy\H{o}ri and Schelp on perfect matchings with prescribed differences. Let $n\ge 2$ and let $d_1,\dots,d_{2^{n-1}}$ be nonzero vectors in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, with repetitions allowed. The space $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ can be partitioned into pairs $\{x_i,y_i\}$ with $x_i+y_i=d_i$ for every $i$ if and only if $\sum_i d_i=0$.
item.dc:creator: Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy (Yohananov)

item.title: On unique realisations of graphs under symmetry constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.32559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Global rigidity asks whether a realisation of a graph is uniquely determined, up to Euclidean congruence, by its edge lengths. In this paper, we study global rigidity of bar-joint frameworks under finite point-group symmetry constraints. A framework is called forced-symmetric globally rigid in $d$-space if every realisation of the graph in $\mathbb R^d$ with the same edge lengths and the same prescribed symmetry is congruent to it. We establish symmetric extensions of two fundamental results on global rigidity. Our first result extends Hendrickson's necessary condition to the forced-symmetric setting. For symmetry-generic frameworks with an arbitrary finite point group acting freely on the vertices and with at least $d+2$ vertex orbits, we prove that forced-symmetric global rigidity implies forced-symmetric redundant rigidity. Our second result extends the classical characterisation of generic global rigidity for body-bar frameworks due to Connelly, Jord\'an and Whiteley. For the symmetric body-bar model considered here, we show that forced-symmetric global rigidity is a generic property and obtain a combinatorial characterisation in every dimension.
item.dc:creator: James Cruickshank, Csaba Kir\'aly, Bernd Schulze, Shin-ichi Tanigawa

item.title: Irreducibility, inertia and invertibility of the eccentricity matrices of unicyclic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.32567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The eccentricity matrix of a connected graph $G$, denoted by $\mathcal{E}(G)$, is obtained from the distance matrix of $G$ by keeping each entry that is the largest in its row or the largest in its column, and replacing all other entries by $0$. The eigenvalues of $\mathcal{E}(G)$ are called the $\mathcal{E}$-eigenvalues of $G$. In this article, we consider the eccentricity matrix of unicyclic graphs and study its various spectral properties. First, we give two sufficient conditions for the irreducibility of the eccentricity matrix of a connected graph, which generalize some previously known results. Then, we show that the eccentricity matrix of every unicyclic graph of girth $3$, $5$ or $7$ is irreducible and provide a unicyclic graph whose eccentricity matrix is reducible for every odd girth $g\ge 9$. On the other hand, we also provide a class of unicyclic graphs of odd girth, whose eccentricity matrices are always irreducible. Additionally, we find the inertia of eccentricity matrices of unicyclic graphs in which the trees attached to the cycle are nontrivial and have equal heights. Moreover, we characterize the graphs in this class whose E-eigenvalues are symmetric about the origin. Finally, we obtain necessary conditions for the invertibility of the eccentricity matrix of a unicyclic graph.
item.dc:creator: Subhendu Chakraborty, Iswar Mahato

item.title: On some off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.32594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a new short proof of a theorem of Fox and He that the $3$-uniform Ramsey number $r_3(K_4^-, K_n)$ is at least $2^{\Omega(n \log n)}$. The construction exploits a new connection with a directed graph recently introduced by Brada\v{c} in his work on off-diagonal graph Ramsey numbers. Moreover, it generalizes naturally to give sharp bounds for several extensions of this problem in higher uniformity, answering questions raised by Mubayi and Suk.
item.dc:creator: Eion Mulrenin, Cosmin Pohoata

item.title: Erd\H{o}s Distance Results for $k$-Degenerate Graphs with $m$ Edges
item.description: arXiv:2611.32669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Erd\H{o}s distinct distances problem asks how many distinct distances $N$ points must determine. In the plane, Guth and Katz determined the optimal power of $N$. A natural generalization fixes a finite graph $G$ with $m$ edges and records, over all injective embeddings of $G$ into a finite point set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, the vectors of edge-lengths realized; we write $\Delta_G^\circ(P)$ for this set of edge-distance vectors. Taking $G$ to be a single edge recovers the classical problem. In the plane, the exponent $|V(G)|-1$ is known up to an arbitrarily small loss for every connected graph. A graph is $k$-degenerate if its vertices can be ordered so that each has at most $k$ neighbors among those preceding it. We show that if $G$ is $k$-degenerate, then for every $d \ge \max(2k,3)$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$, $|\Delta_G^\circ(P)| \gtrsim_{G,d,\varepsilon} N^{m/(d-1)-\varepsilon}$ for $|P|=N\ge |V(G)|$. For a connected graph with $m/(|V(G)|-1)>2(d-1)/d$, the exponent $m/(d-1)$ exceeds the spanning-tree exponent predicted by the pinned-distance conjecture. Our result is motivated by the threshold $\frac{d+k}{2}$ obtained by Borges, Foster, Ou, Palsson, and Romero Acosta for edge lengths of $k$-degenerate graphs in fractal sets. The proof combines a bisector-energy estimate for pinned $k$-stars with an entropy argument of Katz--Tardos type, applied along a construction order of $G$ and combined with an induction on the dimension.
item.dc:creator: Luv Barnwal, Yuda Chen, Eon Lee, Eyvindur Palsson, Braiden Pulver, Steven Senger

item.title: Schnyder Woods and the Chromatic Polynomial
item.description: arXiv:2611.32684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\chi_G(q)$ be the chromatic polynomial of a graph $G$. Analogous to the classical results of Greene and Zaslavsky interpreting $(-1)^{n-1}\chi_G'(0)$ and $(-1)^n\chi_G'(1)$ as counting certain orientations of $G$, we show that if $G$ is a triangulation, $\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{n-1}\chi_G'(2)$ counts the number of Schnyder woods on a plane embedding of $G$. We also generalise this result to graphs obtained by removing certain edges of $G$.
item.dc:creator: Aatman Supkar, Upamanyu Yaddanapudi

item.title: A Classification of Trees Without Unique Subgraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.32711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study trees without unique subgraphs, in both the induced and non-induced settings. Graphs without unique induced subgraphs, called anchor-free graphs, form a natural candidate class for counterexamples to the Graph Reconstruction Conjecture, but their structure remains poorly understood. We develop a framework for studying anchor-free graphs based on a covering lemma that characterizes anchor-freeness via induced subgraph coverings of vertices. Using this framework, we prove that a tree is anchor-free if and only if it is a path with one less vertex than a prime. We also introduce the related notion of unique-subgraph-freeness, which acts as an edge-based analogue of anchor-freeness. We show that the line graph of every unique-subgraph-free graph is anchor-free and obtain a complete classification of unique-subgraph-free trees as either prime paths, stars, or extended stars. Together, these results provide a classification of trees without unique subgraphs and suggest a general approach for extending the theory beyond trees.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Searns

item.title: A degree-sum condition for paths through prescribed vertices
item.description: arXiv:2611.32730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ and let $S\subseteq V(G)$. Denote by $\kappa(S)$ the minimum size of a vertex set separating two vertices of $S$, and by $\sigma_p(S)$ the minimum degree sum over all independent sets of $p$ vertices in $S$. We prove that if $\kappa(S)\ge k\ge2$ and $\sigma_p(S)\ge n+(p-1)^2$ for every integer $p\ge k$, then any two distinct vertices of $S$ are joined by a path containing all vertices of $S$. This gives a path version of Ota's theorem on cycles containing a prescribed set of vertices. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Faudree, Faudree, Gould, Jacobson and Magnant: for $k\ge3$, every $k$-connected graph $G$ of order $n$ satisfying $\delta(G)>(n+k^2-2k)/k$ and $\delta(G)\ge\alpha(G)+k-2$ is hamiltonian-connected.
item.dc:creator: Kun Cheng, Leilei Zhang

item.title: The majority game chromatic number for dense random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.32746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that for every fixed $2/3<p<1$ the majority game chromatic number of the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph $G_{n,p}$ is $3$ with high probability.
item.dc:creator: Stijn Cambie, Annika Heckel, Brahadeesh Sankarnarayanan, Gabri\"elle Zwaneveld

item.title: An Asymptotically Sharp Form of the Overfull Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.32763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph with maximum degree $\Delta$. A subgraph $H$ of $G$ is \emph{$\Delta$-overfull} if $|E(H)|>\Delta\lfloor |V(H)|/2\rfloor$. The Overfull Conjecture, proposed by Chetwynd and Hilton in 1986, states that a graph $G$ with $\Delta>|V(G)|/3$ is of class~2 if and only if it contains a $\Delta$-overfull subgraph. This conjecture would give a polynomial-time algorithm for determining the chromatic index in this degree range and would imply several longstanding conjectures on critical graphs. In this paper, we prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a sufficiently large graph $G$ with $\Delta\ge(1/4+\varepsilon)|V(G)|$ is of class~2 if and only if it contains a $\Delta$-overfull subgraph. Consequently, the chromatic index can be determined in polynomial time in this range. We also obtain the Just-overfull and Vertex-splitting Conjectures for large graphs, and Vizing's Independence Number, Average Degree, and $2$-Factor Conjectures in the same degree range. The coefficient $1/4$ is asymptotically best possible: for every odd integer $\Delta\ge3$, we construct a connected class~2 graph on $4\Delta+5$ vertices with maximum degree $\Delta$ and no $\Delta$-overfull subgraph.
item.dc:creator: Guantao Chen, Songling Shan

item.title: Spanning cyclability of split graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.32794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a positive integer $k$, a graph $G$ is called $k$-spanning cyclable (resp. $k$-edge spanning cyclable) if, given any $k$ distinct vertices $v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_k$ (resp. $k$ independent edges $e_1, e_2, \ldots, e_k$) of $G$, there exist $k$ vertex-disjoint cycles $C_1, C_2, \ldots, C_k$ in $G$ such that $v_i \in V(C_i)$ (resp. $e_i \in E(C_i)$) for each $i$ and $V(C_1) \cup \cdots \cup V(C_k) = V(G)$. In particular, the notion of 1-spanning cyclable coincides with the existence of a Hamiltonian cycle, and a Hamilton-connected graph is necessarily 1-edge spanning cyclable. For a positive integer $r \ge 3$, a graph $G$ is $K_{1,r}$-free if $G$ does not have an induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{1,r}$, and $K_{1,4} + e$ denotes the graph obtained by adding an edge $e$ between two nonadjacent vertices of $K_{1,4}$. There are several interesting conjectures and sparse results relative to these conjectures on Hamiltonian properties of $K_{1,r}$-free split graphs, whose vertex set can be partitioned into a maximum clique $W$ and an independent set $J$. In this paper, we extend some of these results by proving the following: (1) every $(k+1)$-connected $K_{1,3}$-free split graph of order at least $4k-1$ is $k$-spanning cyclable for $k \ge 1$; in particular, every 2-connected $K_{1,3}$-free split graph of order at least 3 is Hamiltonian; (2) every $2k$-connected $K_{1,3}$-free split graph is $k$-edge spanning cyclable for $k \ge 2$; (3) every $(k+1)$-connected $\{K_{1,4}, K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph with $|W| \ge |J| \ge 3k+5$ is $k$-spanning cyclable for $k \ge 1$; in particular, every 2-connected $\{K_{1,4}, K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph with $|W| \ge |J| \ge 8$ is Hamiltonian; (4) every $2k$-connected $\{K_{1,4}, K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph with order at least $4k+9$ is $k$-edge spanning cyclable for $k \ge 2$.
item.dc:creator: Jingfan Zai, Wenjing Lv, Eminjan Sabir

item.title: Even Quartets and the Maximum Density of a Simplical 3-Cocycle
item.description: arXiv:2611.32833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Colour the triples of an $n$-element set red or blue, and call a four-set even if it contains an even number of red triples. We prove that the minimum number of even four-sets is $\frac5{16}\binom n4-\Theta(n^3)$. In particular, the maximum asymptotic density of a simplicial $3$-cocycle over the field of two elements is $11/16$. The classical two-part matrix construction attains the limiting bound. We prove that it also determines the unique limiting distribution of quartet parities on every fixed number of vertices. Writing $m_n$ for the minimum density, we bound the limit inferior and limit superior of $n(5/16-m_n)$ between $0.75$ and $0.752427$. The lower bound on even quartets follows from an exact rational inequality on eight vertices. A perturbation of the construction explains all $72$ cases of equality in this finite inequality, of which only $22$ survive in an extremal limit.
item.dc:creator: John Mackey

item.title: ab-indices for lattice path matroids
item.description: arXiv:2611.32845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The base polytopes of connected lattice path matroids admit subdivisions into snakes. We use these to obtain an explicit positive combinatorial description of their ab-indices, their Chow polynomials and their chain polynomials. We finally apply this description to the particular case of the ab-index of Schubert matroids.
item.dc:creator: Cenk Aydin, Giovanni Caiolo, Chiara Giardino, Mara Gru{\ss}, Mikael H\"aglund, Elena Hoster, Christian Stump

item.title: Analytic properties of Boolean-Narayana numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.32921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Very recently, B\'ona introduced the Boolean-Narayana numbers BoNa(n,k) as the number of 0-1-trees on n+1 vertices with k right edges. We prove the total positivity of the Boolean-Narayana triangle by providing an explicit matrix factorization, and construct a planar digraph for this triangle. We give two combinatorial interpretations of the gamma-coefficients of the Boolean-Narayana polynomials. We also show the strong q-log-convexity of the Boolean-Narayana polynomials and the asymptotic normality of the Boolean-Narayana numbers. A bijection between 0-1-trees and colored Motzkin paths is constructed, presenting an alternative interpretation of the Boolean-Narayana numbers.
item.dc:creator: Xi Chen, Sihao Tang

item.title: Traversing hyperplane arrangements with an affine objective
item.description: arXiv:2611.32976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give geometric constructions of directed acyclic graphs on the chambers of a locally finite affine hyperplane arrangement. Fix a nonconstant affine objective. At each chamber where it is bounded above, a choice of flag based at the optimal face determines $2^r-1$ outgoing edges, where $r$ is the codimension of that face. The optimal value of the objective weakly increases on each step, but not always strictly. Nevertheless, we show that every infinite directed walk in these graphs eventually reaches a chamber where the optimal value exceeds its starting value. Additionally, we show that if an affine objective is bounded above on a closed face of a locally finite affine hyperplane arrangement, then the supremum is attained, and the optimizer set is again a closed face, generalizing the classical result for polyhedra.
item.dc:creator: Brennan Dury

item.title: Triangle-free planar graphs need not be POSH
item.description: arXiv:2611.32999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a triangle-free planar graph need not be partial one-sided Hamiltonian. This disproves a conjecture of Felsner, Schrezenmaier, Schr\"oder and Steiner.
item.dc:creator: Mykhaylo Tyomkyn

item.title: Undershoot of h-fold sumsets: Ap\'ery spectra, similar ordering and the three-distance theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.33046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite set $A_0\subset\mathbb{N}$ with $0\in A_0$, $\max A_0=d$ and $\gcd(A_0)=1$, and a target $T$, the undershoot at level $h$ is the distance from $T$ down to the largest element of the $h$-fold sumset $hA_0$ not above $T$. Its total over $T\in[0,hd]$ is bounded in $h$: for large $h$ it equals the sum of the masses of two numerical semigroups attached to $A_0$, where the mass adds $L(L+1)/2$ over the maximal runs of $L$ gaps. We describe how the total reaches this limit: it can rise to it, fall to it, or climb past it and return. When the monomial curve of $A_0$ is arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay, two Ap\'ery sets give every undershoot exactly, and partial sums of a fixed spectrum bound the total from below, with equality at every level exactly when two threshold sequences are similarly ordered; the total then rises concavely to its limit, reached exactly at the sumsets regularity. We characterize the similarly ordered four-element sets. For $\{0,a,b,2b\}$ with $0<a<b$ coprime, the three-distance theorem gives the total in explicit quadratic pieces. A non-Cohen-Macaulay set exceeds its limit at every failing level $h$ with $hd$ at least the sum of the two conductors; every such four-element set does so, and a five-element example never does. For arbitrary sets, finite corner data give the exact undershoot over any window.
item.dc:creator: Prashant Chaudhary, Kapil Khandelwal

item.title: Large blow-ups of uniform hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.33108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(k\ge2\), let \(H\) be a fixed \(k\)-uniform hypergraph on \(h\) vertices with at least one edge, and let \(a>0\). We prove that every sufficiently large \(n\)-vertex \(k\)-uniform hypergraph with at least \(a n^h\) copies of \(H\) contains a blow-up of \(H\) with at least \(b(\log n)^{1/(k-1)}\) vertices in each part, where \(b=b(H,a)>0\). The exponent of $\log n$ is best possible. This answers a question of R\"odl and Schacht and proves a conjecture of Bollob\'as, Erd\H{o}s and Simonovits from 1976. For fixed \(q\ge2\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\), it follows that every \(q\)-coloring of the \(k\)-subsets of \([n]\) contains a set of order \((\log n)^{1/(k-1)}\) on which one color has density at least \(1-\alpha\). For triples this recovers the sharp bound of Conlon, Fox and Sudakov. For \(k\ge4\), this improves their general exponent to the optimal value \(1/(k-1)\) and answers a 1990 question of Erd\H{o}s for which he offered a \$500 prize.
item.dc:creator: Dhruv Mubayi

item.title: Efficient reconfiguration, polynomial decompositions and approximate counting
item.description: arXiv:2611.33120v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider reconfigurations of integer assignments to planar lattice regions that preserve specified line totals, which are motivated by questions of combinatorial construction, algorithmic sampling and approximate counting. An elementary prototype is provided by contingency tables, i.e. two-dimensional grids of non-negative integers with prescribed row and column sums, which can be reconfigured by basic switches of the form $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. More difficult combinatorial instances include reconfiguration of Latin squares or queens configurations. Our main technical ingredient is the following polynomial decomposition lemma. Fix a positive integer $k$. Let $F(x)\in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be a polynomial of degree at most $n$ such that $(1-x)^k\mid F(x)$ and the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients of $F$ is $m$. We prove that $F$ can be written as a sum of $O(m+n)$ basic polynomials of degree at most $n$ of the form $\pm x^a(1-x^{a_1})\cdots (1-x^{a_k})$ where $a,a_1,\ldots,a_k$ are non-negative integers. The proof uses the existence of a miraculous high-dimensional coupling of signed distributions on cross polytopes that has independent interest. We will apply this lemma to questions of combinatorial construction in other papers; in this paper we illustrate its application to approximate counting.
item.dc:creator: Peter Keevash, Jeck Lim

item.title: A canonical Euclidean Gallai theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.33136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we prove a canonical Euclidean Gallai theorem: for any finite set of points $S\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, any colouring of $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a scaled (and possibly rotated) copy of $S$ that is either monochromatic or rainbow.
item.dc:creator: Benedict Randall Shaw

item.title: Dominoes tiling a common figure
item.description: arXiv:2611.33154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Call a two-element subset of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ a domino. Given finitely many dominoes $D_1,\ldots,D_k$, we show that there exists a finite non-empty $B\subset \mathbb{Z}^2$ such that $B$ can be partitioned into disjoint translates of $D_i$ for all $i$. The proof uses a new absorption mechanism for perfect matchings in algebraically defined hypergraphs.
item.dc:creator: Peter Keevash, Jeck Lim

item.title: Depth of leaves in closed linear $\lambda$-terms: exact recurrence, limit law and edge window
item.description: arXiv:2611.31323v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K_n$ (resp.\ $D_n$) be the depth of a uniform leaf (resp.\ node) in a uniform closed linear $\lambda$-term of size $n$. A bijective \emph{grafting identity} yields an exact polynomial-time recurrence for the full depth profile. By the method of moments, $K_n/n$ converges in law to the density $3x/\sqrt{1-2x}$ on $[0,\frac12]$, i.e.\ $2K_n/n\to\Beta(2,\frac12)$, with $\mathbb E[K_n^r]/n^r\to3(r+1)!/(2r+3)!!$; likewise $1-2D_n/n\to\Beta(\frac12,1)$. A backward Markov chain gives the corresponding local limits for $k\le(\frac12-\varepsilon)n$. The limit density diverges at $\frac12$, and the profile has a second scale: a window of width $\sqrt n$ around $n/2$, which carries a fraction of order $n^{-1/4}$ of the nodes, at a density $n^{1/4}$ times larger than in the bulk. We prove that a single explicit function describes both regimes: uniformly in $d$, \[ n^{3/4}\,\mathbb P(D_n=d)=g\Bigl(\tfrac{d-n/2}{\sqrt n}\Bigr)+O(n^{-1/16}),\qquad n^{3/4}\,\mathbb P(K_n=d)=\tfrac{3d}{n}\,g\Bigl(\tfrac{d-n/2}{\sqrt n}\Bigr)+O(n^{-1/16}), \] where $g(y)=2^{-1/2}e^{-y^2}D_{-1/2}(2y)$ is a parabolic cylinder function. In particular $\mathbb P(K_n>n/2)\sim\frac34\,\mathbb E|Z|^{1/2}\,n^{-1/4}\approx0.6166\,n^{-1/4}$ with $Z$ standard Gaussian. The proofs rest on harmonic functions of the heat equation evaluated along the backward chain.
item.dc:creator: Olivier Bodini (LAGA)

item.title: Ternary Perfect $2$-Burst-Correcting Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.31328v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A construction for a ternary perfect linear $2$-burst-correcting code is presented for every redundancy $r \geq 5$. The construction is recursive with seeds given for $5 \leq r \leq 7$. The construction of redundancy $r \geq 8$ is derived from a code of redundancy $r-3$ and it distinguishes between codes of even and odd length.
item.dc:creator: Tuvi Etzion

item.title: Partition growth homomorphisms on Specht modules
item.description: arXiv:2611.31510v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: There is a unique (up to scalar) representation homomorphism between the Specht modules $\mathcal{S}^\lambda$ and $\mathcal{S}^\mu$ when $\mu$ is obtained from $\lambda$ by adding one to a part of $\lambda$. We find explicit formulas for these homomorphisms in the Specht polynomial bases of $\mathcal{S}^\lambda$ and $\mathcal{S}^\mu$. Furthermore, given two representation homomorphisms corresponding to adding one to two different parts of $\lambda$, we find the commutator for the composition of these two homomorphisms. We also extend the Specht polynomial basis of $\mathcal{S}^\lambda$ into a basis of the permutation module $\mathcal{H}^\lambda$ and explicitly find a formula for the skew isomorphism from $\mathcal{S}^\lambda$ to $\mathcal{S}^{\lambda'}$.
item.dc:creator: Aar\'on Ocampo

item.title: Schubert positivity for filtered bundles
item.description: arXiv:2611.31862v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterize formal filtered nefness of a formal quotient flag on a polarized Hodge--Lefschetz module by the formal nefness of its positive-rank total quotients. Using this criterion, we prove that quotient Schubert functors preserve formal nefness and that Schubert incidence modules inherit every commuting formally filtered nef flag. As geometric and numerical consequences, we recover the positivity criteria of Fulton--Lazarsfeld and Fulton and extend the Lorentzian polynomial theorem of Lu and Zheng to derived Schubert classes of filtered bundles. In combinatorics, our framework applies to tautological flags of flag matroids on ordinary and augmented matroid Chow rings as well as on the intersection cohomology of rational projective fans equipped with a common weight map. We deduce concordance-sensitive intersection inequalities, establish the Schubert positivity of the leading Riemann--Roch Chow class of a flag matroid, and show that the nonvanishing supports of derived Schubert numbers on an augmented Chow ring form the Higgs lifts of an intrinsically determined matroid quotient.
item.dc:creator: Enhan Li

item.title: Linear programming certificates for dimension bounds of hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2611.31913v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use linear programming to derive upper bounds for the dimension of hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes from local geometric and arithmetic estimates. Rational certificates give the bounds $57$ for finite-volume polytopes, $17$ for compact polytopes, and $15$ for compact arithmetic polytopes. In the finite-volume case, the certificate is a weight function on incidences between vertices and two-dimensional faces. In the compact cases, the inequalities concern squared norms of orthogonal projections of a fixed tangent vector at a vertex farthest from an interior point. We give a common formulation of these linear programs, prove monotonicity in the dimension threshold, and describe the exact verification of the certificates. The local estimates are taken from the companion geometric proofs.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Kolpakov

item.title: Finiteness and completeness of $g$-fans for real-weighted quivers
item.description: arXiv:2611.31946v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study finiteness and completeness of $g$-fans for quivers with positive real weights. We characterize finite Coxeter type by the condition that every weight in the mutation class has the form $2\cos(\pi/m)$ for some integer $m\geq3$. Under total sign-coherence, we then show that a quiver with finitely many $g$-clusters is $2$-finite, that is, every weight in its mutation class is less than $2$. This also gives a new proof that $g$-finiteness implies finite Coxeter type. Assuming in addition that, for every initial quiver in the mutation class, each $c$-vector on a coordinate axis is a signed standard basis vector, we prove that the $g$-fan is complete if and only if there are finitely many $g$-clusters. The main geometric result states that the coordinate projection of every $g$-cone is contained in a $g$-cone of the corresponding full subquiver. Consequently, completeness and density pass to full subquivers.
item.dc:creator: Ryota Akagi, Toshiya Yurikusa

item.title: The Generalized Volterra Signature
item.description: arXiv:2611.31967v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the generalized Volterra signature \(\gvsig(\bX)\) of a path \(\bX\), extending the classical Volterra signature introduced in [Hager, Harang, Pelizzari \& Tindel, arXiv:2603.04525, 2026], which extends Lyons' path signature to the Volterra setting. We establish a new algebraic structure to encode the generalized Volterra signature. We also establish a generalized Chen's identity. By restricting the differential trees to ladder trees, we introduce the geometric Volterra signature \(\geovsig(\bX)\) and establish the shuffle product of its signature components. To the best of our knowledge, the shuffle product for the Volterra signature is the first of its kind and allows us to formulate a universal approximation theorem for geometric Volterra signatures. For a special class of kernel functions, we prove the existence of an extended path \(\Bar{\bX}\) and relate its classical signature to the geometric Volterra signature of the original path \(\bX\).
item.dc:creator: Munawar Ali, Qi Feng, Samy Tindel

item.title: Alexander modules and Milnor fibers of topological line arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2611.32339v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Alexander module and a distinguished cyclic cover, which we call the \textit{topological Milnor fiber}, of the complements of topological line arrangements. For every topologically realizable combinatorial type with $n \geq 2$ lines, where $n$ is not a prime power, we prove that the first Betti numbers of its topological Milnor fibers are unbounded. Moreover, any finite abelian group occurs as a direct summand of the integral homology of a topological Milnor fiber within the given combinatorial type. As an application, we show that every topologically realizable combinatorial type with $n \geq 2$ lines admits a realization whose complement has no $2$-dimensional CW model.
item.dc:creator: Sakumi Sugawara

item.title: Counting tree-child and reticulation visible networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.32460v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For tree-child networks with $n$ leaves and $k$ reticulations, we identify an entire critical scaling function at $k=x\sqrt n$ and its first uniform correction. The function is a Gaussian factor times the Laplace transform of Brownian excursion area. An exact coefficient integral then yields the explicit amplitude $\pi\Ai'(a_1)$ for the maximal-reticulation count, where $a_1$ is the largest negative Airy zero, together with three logarithmic corrections. A summable defect expansion transfers these results to the total number of tree-child networks. For reticulation-visible networks, we construct an exact weighted refinement over maximal tree-child networks. The total defect from $3n-3$ reticulations splits into a skeleton defect, an arity excess, and an ordinary-leaf count. The skeleton defect has a uniformly bounded exponential moment, and the full partition function differs from its maximal-skeleton sector by a bounded factor, smaller than $30$ at activity one. A positive algebraic kernel and an explicitly solved variational problem give the pressure with logarithmic error $O(n^{2/3}\log^{2/3}n)$. This determines the total exponential growth, the location of every mode, a full large-deviation principle, and limiting structural densities. At activity $z=t/n$ with fixed $t>0$, we also prove a $\operatorname{Poisson}(19t/4)$ limit and coefficient asymptotics uniform for defects $q=o(n^{1/3})$.
item.dc:creator: Miquel Pons Viver

item.title: The Min-Cut Formulation of Ollivier-Ricci Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2611.32528v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computing Ollivier-Ricci curvature normally requires a local distance matrix and a linear program per edge, prompting workarounds based on entropic regularization or combinatorial proxies. We show that exact curvature needs neither. For any one-step measures, the Kantorovich dual has an integral three-level optimum, reducing each edge to one minimum s-t cut on a distance-free network linear in the read adjacency lists. This solves instances requiring quadratically many distance queries in linear time, while a converse reduction shows that no exact algorithm can beat bipartite matching. Our solver is a median 6 times (up to 506 times) faster than distance construction plus $\mathtt{POT}$'s C++ simplex, 441 times faster than $\mathtt{GraphRicciCurvature}$, and 23 times faster than graph min-cost flow. Even given the distances, Sinkhorn iterations at $\mathtt{GraphRicciCurvature}$'s regularization are a median 12 times slower, and combinatorial proxies alter edge rankings, missing the bulk of the most negatively curved ones.
item.dc:creator: Giorgio Micaletto

item.title: Theta Functions and Intrinsic Mirrors of Laurent Phenomenon Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.32571v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct bases of upper Laurent phenomenon algebras over a field by minimizing Newton polytopes in a single seed. For any translation-invariant total order on the exponents, each least exponent $a$ that occurs determines a smallest Newton polytope $Q_a$. Choose one element with Newton polytope $Q_a$ and least term $x^a$ for each such $a$. These elements form a basis. In every reachable seed chart, every Gauss valuation takes a nonzero basis expansion to the minimum of its values on the nonzero summands. Suppose the algebra has Laurent coefficients and smooth spectrum over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. After setting the curve parameters to one, we compute theta products on the intrinsic mirror from the exchange polynomials and give a finite presentation of the mirror algebra. A seed has a polynomial corner if each exchange polynomial can be multiplied by a unit of the coefficient ring to give a polynomial with constant term one. At such a corner, order the exponents by a weight with strictly positive, rationally independent coordinates. For every lattice exponent $a$ and integral weight $p$, the theta function indexed by $p$ has least $a$-weight $\min_{b\in Q_a}\langle b,p\rangle$ in the corresponding mirror chart. This reciprocity holds for cyclic exchanges and arbitrary pole orders. For fixed exchange supports and constant terms one, we determine when the mirror is smooth and the second mirror recovers the original algebra in the chosen torus coordinates. The coefficient tuples for which both conditions hold form a computable finite set. All their entries are positive integers.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Fei

item.title: Sparse Additive Spanners and the Cost Spectra of Group Actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32607v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How sparse can a Cayley graph become if we retain all its vertices and allow distances to increase by at most a fixed additive constant? We study invariant random spanning subgraphs, measuring sparsity by the expected degree at a vertex. On the square grid, a random translate of a sparse mesh brings the mean degree arbitrarily close to two. If the choice must be made equivariantly from independent vertex labels, every edge is forced. In this expository note we follow these two answers through other groups. Geometry alone forces a positive gap on each non-elementary hyperbolic Cayley graph, while on one four-regular nilpotent Cayley graph the choice of action realizes every additive cost in $[1,2]$. The minimum of the action spectrum recovers the geometric cost. Open problems are presented in the end.
item.dc:creator: Itai Benjamini

item.title: Unbounded GHZ dimension from fixed-order multiphoton sources
item.description: arXiv:2611.32673v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the local dimension of Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) states obtained by selecting events with one photon per output path. Each coherent source emits photons with a fixed internal label into a distinct set of paths, and the sets for each label partition the outputs. For two-photon sources, the maximum local dimension is 2 for every even number of paths greater than 4. However, we show that three-photon sources can produce GHZ states of arbitrarily large local dimension. To prove this, we view the three paths fed by each source as an edge of a $3$-uniform hypergraph, so that accepted emission patterns correspond exactly to perfect matchings. We construct such hypergraphs with arbitrarily many edge-disjoint perfect matchings, one per label, and no others. The construction extends to $r$-uniform hypergraphs for every fixed $r\ge3$, yielding a GHZ dimension that grows at least polynomially as the number of paths ranges over the positive multiples of $r$.
item.dc:creator: Heng Li, Xizhi Liu

item.title: Temporal Inhomogeneous Random Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.32717v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by the study of time-dependent propagation processes in inhomogeneous populations, we extend Burova, Lugosi and Perarnau's results on the temporal stochastic block model to graphon-based random graphs with a continuous and strictly positive kernel. We consider such a graph in the regime where connection probabilities are of the order of $\log n/n$, and equip its edges with a uniformly random ordering, interpreted as timestamps. We study the size of reachable sets via increasing paths (that is, paths whose edge timestamps are strictly increasing). We establish tight first-order asymptotics for the size of the reachable set from a fixed vertex, and also determine the first-order asymptotics of the lengths of the longest and shortest increasing paths with one or two fixed endpoints.
item.dc:creator: Sofiya Burova, Francisco Calvillo

item.title: Fluctuations in the k-cut numbers of random recursive trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.32740v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the k-cut procedure introduced by Cai et al. [EJP, 2018] on random recursive trees. Our main result identifies the fluctuations in the number of cuts required to isolate the root as the tree size tends to infinity. This extends the results by Drmota et al. [RSA, 2009] and Iksanov et al. [ECP, 2007] for the classical cutting procedure.
item.dc:creator: Laura Eslava, Marco L. Ortiz, Minmin Wang

item.title: A short proof of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.32872v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a short alternative proof of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture, recently proved by OpenAI. Our proof combines their reduction with a different argument showing that every nontrivial oriented graph $G$ contains a nonempty set $X$ such that $X^+\ne V(G)$ and $|(X^+)^+\setminus X^+|\geq|X^+\setminus X|$, where $X^+=N_G^+[X]$.
item.dc:creator: Romain Bourneuf, Pierre Charbit, Samuel Coulomb, St\'ephan Thomass\'e

item.title: Convexification effects of $L_p$-sums
item.description: arXiv:2611.32879v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is a classical result, quantified by Shapley, Folkman, and Starr, that the Minkowski averages of any compact set asymptotically approach its convex hull in the Hausdorff metric. In this paper, we investigate the analogous convexification phenomenon for the Firey $L_p$-sums of compact sets. First, we establish new structural properties of the $L_p$-sum. Notably, we show that the iterated $L_p$-sum of compact sets whose convex hull contains the origin is eventually starlike. We then study $L_p$-convexification for three classical measures of nonconvexity: Hausdorff metric, volume deficit, and effective standard deviation. For each of these measures, we prove that the $k$-fold $L_p$-sum averages of a compact set $A$ converge to $\text{conv}(0,A)$ when $1<p<\infty$, and to $\text{conv}(A)$ when $p=\infty$. In each case, we show that the convergence to the convex hull is eventually monotone. For the Hausdorff metric and effective standard deviation, we prove sharp upper bounds for the $L_p$-sum of two compact sets.
item.dc:creator: Matthieu Fradelizi, Auttawich Manui, Mark Meyer, Maud Szusterman, Artem Zvavitch

item.title: Positive Geometry of Oriented Matroid Strata
item.description: arXiv:2611.32956v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the positive geometry of Grassmannians whose boundary is a union of Pl\"ucker divisors. For the full Pl\"ucker boundary the regions are closures of realization spaces of uniform oriented matroids. In rank three we show that the pair $(\mathrm{Gr}_{3,n},Z_{3,n})$ is a positive arrangement in the sense of Sturmfels and Telen for $n\le 9$ points and compute its combinatorial rank from point counts of the configuration space $\mathcal{X}_{3,n}$ over finite fields. For seven points the canonical forms of the regions span all logarithmic forms. For eight points they do not, because the M\"obius-Kantor configuration is not realizable over the reals. This determines for seven and eight points whether the integrands of Cachazo, Early and Zhang for the generalized biadjoint amplitudes of Cachazo, Early, Guevara and Mizera span the space of logarithmic forms. From ten points on, the genus is positive because a K3 surface appears in the boundary. For smaller boundaries and arbitrary rank we give a recursion that adds one point at a time and preserves the genus and the combinatorial rank. It recovers the positive Grassmannian and shows that realization spaces of stacked polytopes are regions of positive arrangements of combinatorial rank one.
item.dc:creator: Arne Kuhrs, Artyom Lisitsyn

item.title: Boomerang identities and binomial transform
item.description: arXiv:2611.32965v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In Pascal's triangle, the boomerang identities, which were recently introduced, combine and extend the well-known hockey-stick identities of the binomial coefficients by allowing additional terms. We show that the binomial transform of sequences in a ring play a central role in this context. Subsequently, we show several applications to Bell and Bernoulli numbers and polynomials, Appell polynomials, as well as, to harmonic, Fibonacci, Lucas, and Stirling numbers.
item.dc:creator: Bernd C. Kellner

item.title: $S$-preclones and the Galois connection ${}^S\mathrm{Pol}$-${}^S\mathrm{Inv}$, Part II: Boolean $\pm$-preclones
item.description: arXiv:2611.33066v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We continue the investigation of $S$-preclones initiated in Part I, specializing to the case of Boolean $\pm$-preclones where $S = \{+,-\}$ is the two-element group and the base set is $A = \{0,1\}$. The main results include the complete classification of maximal and minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones in the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ of all Boolean $\pm$-preclones. We prove that there are exactly nine maximal Boolean $\pm$-preclones. Hence we obtain a completeness theorem for $\pm$-preclones: a set of $\pm$-operations generates all $\pm$-operations if and only if it contains an operation that fails to preserve each of the nine defining $\pm$-relations of the maximal $\pm$-preclones. Next we classify the twenty minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones (atoms of the lattice), each described via a generating $\pm$-operation. We also investigate self-dual $\pm$-preclones, characterizing the eight maximal and nine minimal self-dual $\pm$-preclones and proving a corresponding completeness theorem. Additionally, we include the result, due to Vojt\v{e}ch David, that the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ is uncountable, in contrast with the countability of the classical Post lattice of Boolean clones. This is established by embedding an uncountable poset of clonoids into ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$. Finally, we study preimage classes of classical Boolean clones within ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$, providing complete descriptions for the unary case and for several non-unary minimal clones. We also prove a Baker--Pixley type theorem for $\pm$-preclones containing the majority operation, showing that such $\pm$-preclones are determined by their binary $\pm$-relations.
item.dc:creator: Peter Jipsen, Erkko Lehtonen, Reinhard P\"oschel

item.title: The tower transition in majority bootstrap percolation
item.description: arXiv:2611.33087v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How large must a high-dimensional torus be for majority bootstrap percolation to fill it at a given density below one half? For a torus of side length $n\ge3$, let $H(n)$ be the smallest $h$ such that a tower of $h$ twos has value at least $n$. If $H(n)/d\to\rho\in[0,1]$, the critical density on the $d$-dimensional torus tends to $(1-\rho)/(2-\rho)$. In particular, the smallest side length $n$ for which the critical density is at most $1/4$ satisfies $H(n)\sim 2d/3$. The same curve holds for ordinary boxes of side at least $d$. For boxes with $n/d\to a>0$ we obtain the limiting density $\max\{1/2,1-2^{-1/a}\}$. We determine the first correction to the tower curve away from $\rho=1$.
item.dc:creator: Vyacheslav Koval, Yuval Peres

item.title: Max-degree filtration, Koszul complexes, and Multicolor Permutation Wordle
item.description: arXiv:2611.33113v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We explore the Koszul resolutions of a family of ideals, each generated by multivariate polynomials that split completely into linear factors. The motivating examples come from the game Permutation Wordle of Kutin and Smithline, as analyzed by Kutin, Smithline, and Vatter, and an open question, Conjecture 4.5 in Kutin and Smithline's work on Multicolor Permutation Wordle. For each ideal in this family, with our chosen generators, the Koszul differentials are strict for the max-degree filtration and, more generally, at every multidegree whose coordinates form a set of consecutive integers. The resulting dimension count resolves Kutin and Smithline's conjecture. The proof is an induction in which each inductive step is an iteration. The core argument is human generated. The present proof, developed with AI assistance, separates the iteration of multidegree reductions from the mapping cone induction. This method avoids the need to chase compatibility of lifts up to the top grade of the complex.
item.dc:creator: Lawren M. Smithline

item.title: Winning and losing NoGo is PSPACE-complete
item.description: arXiv:2611.33127v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We resolve an open problem of Burke and Hearn and show that the combinatorial game NoGo is PSPACE-complete on grids. This is the usual geometry the game is played on, including at the tournament at a 2011 Banff workshop. In addition to this result, we show that it is also PSPACE-complete under mis\`ere play on grids. We prove both of these results using reductions from Bounded Two-Player Constraint Logic. Finally, we show that it is PSPACE-complete under normal play on connected bipartite subcubic graphs.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Burke, Alfie Davies, Craig Tennenhouse

item.title: The transversal game
item.description: arXiv:2401.16768v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two players take turns claiming empty cells from an $n\times n$ grid. The first player (if any) to occupy a transversal (a set of $ n $ cells having no two cells in the same row or column) is the winner. What is the outcome of the game given optimal play? Our aim in this paper is to show that for $n\ge 4$ the first player has a winning strategy. This answers a question of Erickson. We also consider variants of the game in which the family of winning transversals is restricted, both in the original game and in its Maker--Breaker version.
item.dc:creator: \v{Z}arko Ran{\dj}elovi\'c

item.title: Quickly excluding an apex-forest
item.description: arXiv:2404.17306v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a short proof that for every apex-forest $X$ on at least two vertices, graphs excluding $X$ as a minor have layered pathwidth at most $2|V(X)|-3$. This improves upon a result by Dujmovi\'c, Eppstein, Joret, Morin, and Wood (SIDMA, 2020). Our main tool is a structural result about graphs excluding a forest as a rooted minor, which is of independent interest. We develop similar tools for treedepth and treewidth. We discuss implications for Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa properties of rooted models of minors in graphs.
item.dc:creator: J\k{e}drzej Hodor, Hoang La, Piotr Micek, Cl\'ement Rambaud

item.title: Non-solvable $2$-arc-transitive covers of the Petersen graph
item.description: arXiv:2503.06979v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While solvable covers of 2-arc-transitive graphs have been studied extensively, non-solvable covers have remained largely unexplored. This paper takes a first step by constructing such covers for the Petersen graph and determining their structural properties.
item.dc:creator: Jiyong Chen, Cai Heng Li, Ci Xuan Wu, Yan Zhou Zhu

item.title: Hamilton cycles in pseudorandom graphs: resilience and approximate decompositions
item.description: arXiv:2507.22807v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dirac's classical theorem asserts that, for $n\ge 3$, any $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree at least $\frac{n}{2}$ is Hamiltonian. Furthermore, if we additionally assume that such graphs are regular and sufficiently large, then, by the breakthrough work of Csaba, K\"uhn, Lo, Osthus, and Treglown, they admit a decomposition into Hamilton cycles and at most one perfect matching, solving the well-known Nash-Williams conjecture. In the pseudorandom setting, it has long been conjectured that similar results hold in much sparser graphs. We prove two overarching theorems for graphs that exclude excessively dense subgraphs, which yield asymptotically optimal resilience and Hamilton-decomposition results in sparse pseudorandom graphs. First, our results imply that for every fixed $\gamma>0$, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that if $G$ is a spanning subgraph of an $(n,d,\lambda)$-graph satisfying $\delta(G)\ge\bigl(\tfrac12+\gamma\bigr)d$ and $ d/\lambda\ge C,$ then $G$ must contain a Hamilton cycle. Second, we show that for every $\varepsilon>0$, there is $C>0$ so that any $(n,d,\lambda)$-graph $G$ with $d/\lambda\ge C$ contains at least $\bigl(1-\varepsilon\bigr)\tfrac d2$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles, and, finally, we prove that the entire edge set of $G$ can be covered by no more than $\bigl(1+\varepsilon\bigr)\tfrac d2$ such cycles. All bounds are asymptotically optimal and significantly improve earlier results on Hamiltonian resilience, packing, and covering in sparse pseudorandom graphs.
item.dc:creator: Nemanja Dragani\'c, Jaehoon Kim, Hyunwoo Lee, David Munh\'a Correia, Mat\'ias Pavez-Sign\'e, Benny Sudakov

item.title: Fractional domatic number and minimum degree
item.description: arXiv:2508.19617v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The domatic number of a graph $G$ is the maximum number of pairwise disjoint dominating sets of $G$. We are interested in the LP-relaxation of this parameter, which is called the fractional domatic number of $G$. We study its extremal value in the class of graphs of minimum degree $d$. The fractional domatic number of a graph of minimum degree $d$ is always at most $d+1$, and at least $(1-o(1))\, d/\ln d$ as $d\to \infty$. This is asymptotically tight even within the class of split graphs. Our main result concerns the case $d=2$; we show that, excluding $8$ exceptional graphs, the fractional domatic number of every connected graph of minimum degree (at least) $2$ is at least $5/2$. We also show that this bound cannot be improved if only finitely many graphs are excluded, even for bipartite graphs of arbitrarily large girth. This proves in a stronger sense a conjecture by Gadouleau, Harms, Mertzios, and Zamaraev (2024). This also extends and generalises results from McCuaig and Shepherd (1989), from Fujita, Kameda, and Yamashita (2000), and from Abbas, Egerstedt, Liu, Thomas, and Whalen (2016). Finally, we show that graphs of sub-exponential expansion and sufficiently large girth $g$ have fractional domatic number $3 - o_g(1)$.
item.dc:creator: Quentin Chuet, Hugo Demaret, Hoang La, Fran\c{c}ois Pirot

item.title: Lexical tableaux and quasisymmetric functions
item.description: arXiv:2511.00713v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce dual lexical functions, which we construct as an iterated strict-minimum restricted product on Frobenius characteristics of the trivial representation of the cyclic group induced to the symmetric group, generalizing Grinberg's construction of the dual immaculate functions. To model these combinatorially, we introduce lexical tableaux, a generalization of immaculate tableaux in which each row is lexicographically minimal among its cyclic shifts. For a fixed shape, standard lexical tableaux can be counted by a hook length formula with a q-analogue, while summing over all shapes with a fixed size and number of rows gives the (q-)Stirling numbers of the first kind. The dual lexical functions are then the generating functions of lexical tableaux, and they form a basis of the quasisymmetric functions. The dual lexical functions have a positive expansion into the fundamental basis, with coefficients counting another new family of tableaux defined by conditions on the major index values of their rows. We also introduce column-strict lexical tableaux and their respective quasisymmetric functions. We show that standard column-strict lexical tableaux are in bijection with multidimensional Kreweras-type lattice paths.
item.dc:creator: John M. Campbell, Spencer Daugherty

item.title: An improved bound on the Overfull Conjecture for graphs with small minimum degree and large maximum degree
item.description: arXiv:2512.07044v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph with order $n$, maximum degree $\Delta(G)$, minimum degree $\delta(G)$, and chromatic index $\chi'(G)$. A graph $G$ is called $\Delta$-critical if $\chi'(G)=\Delta(G)+1$ and $\chi'(H) < \chi'(G)$ for every proper subgraph $H$ of $G$, and $G$ is overfull if $\left|E(G)\right|>\Delta(G)\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\rfloor$. In 1986, Chetwynd and Hilton proposed the Overfull Conjecture, which is equivalent to the following $\Delta$-critical form: Every $\Delta$-critical graph $G$ with $\Delta(G) > \frac{n}{3}$ is overfull. The Overfull Conjecture has many implications. For example, it implies a polynomial-time algorithm for determining the chromatic index of graphs $G$ with $\Delta(G) > \frac{n}{3}$, and implies several longstanding conjectures in the area of graph edge coloring. Recently, Cao, Chen, Jing, and Shan (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2022) verified the Overfull Conjecture for $\Delta$-critical graphs $G$ when $\Delta(G)-\frac{7\delta(G)}{4}\ge \frac{3n-17}{4}$. In this paper, we establish the required bound $\Delta(G)-\frac{5\delta(G)}{3}\ge\frac{2n-7}{3}$.
item.dc:creator: Xuli Qi, Chunhui Ge, Yanrui Feng

item.title: Online Ramsey numbers of the claw versus cycles
item.description: arXiv:2601.05452v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The online Ramsey number $\tilde r(G,H)$ is defined via a Builder--Painter game on an empty graph with countably many vertices. In each round, Builder reveals an edge, which Painter immediately colors either red or blue. Builder wins once a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$ appears, and $\tilde r(G,H)$ is the minimum number of edges Builder must reveal to force a win. For a long cycle $C_\ell$, the online Ramsey numbers $\tilde r(G,C_\ell)$ are known only for a few specific choices of $G$. In particular, exact values were determined for $G=P_3$ by Cyman, Dzido, Lapinskas, and Lo (Electron. J. Combin., 2015), while asymptotically tight results were obtained when $G$ is an even cycle by Adamski, Bednarska-Bzd\c{e}ga, and Bla\v{z}ej (SIAM J. Discrete Math., 2024).
