In this paper, we consider the case where $G$ is the claw $K_{1,3}$ and determine the exact value of $\tilde r(K_{1,3},C_\ell)$. We show that \[ \tilde r(K_{1,3},C_\ell)=\left\lfloor \frac{3(\ell+1)}{2} \right\rfloor \quad \text{for all } \ell \ge 13. \]
item.dc:creator: Hexuan Zhi, Yanbo Zhang

item.title: Subword enumeration up to stack-sorting equivalence
item.description: arXiv:2604.25811v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Defant and Kravitz introduced generalizations of West's stack-sorting map $s$ from permutations to finite words. This raises questions as to how such generalizations could be applied in the field of combinatorics on words. The Defant-Kravitz generalizations of $s$ depend on how repeated occurrences of the same character within a word may be repositioned, according to their $\textsf{tortoise}$ and $\textsf{hare}$ operations. As demonstrated in this paper, these operations provide a natural way of extending abelian complexity functions for infinite sequences, in a way that gives light to structural properties associated with infinite words. We apply these new ideas to two famous infinite words: the paperfolding word and the Thue-Morse word. In the case of the Thue-Morse word, we discover an interesting connection to the previous work of several authors, such as de Luca and Varricchio, on the ``special'' factors of the Thue-Morse word. This may be seen as providing a basis for a new and interdisciplinary area linking the combinatorics about the stack-sorting of permutations with the field of combinatorics on words.
item.dc:creator: John M. Campbell, Narad Rampersad

item.title: $L^p$-form of the KNRS conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2606.30010v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $F$ be a graph with $m>0$ edges and $n$ non-isolated vertices. For every $\rho$-locally dense graphon $W$, we prove that $\|W_F\|_q\ge\rho^m$ whenever $q\ge\binom n2/m$, where $W_F$ is the product of $W$ over the edges of $F$. The KNRS conjecture asks for this bound at $q=1$. More generally, averaging over the automorphisms of an edge-transitive KNRS supergraph $J$ yields the sufficient exponent $e(J)/m$; for $\rho>0$ and $q>e(J)/m$, equality holds only for constant graphons. The proof averages over vertex relabellings via H\"older's inequality, in the spirit of Conlon and Lee. We also prove that replacing every edge of a Sidorenko-good graph by a fixed theta pattern preserves goodness for all branch lengths, and that applying the same substitution to a KNRS graph yields a regular-KNRS graph. For non-uniform substitutions, we establish goodness under the branch-count conditions of Im, Li, and Liu and determine when equality forces the kernel to be constant. Passing to the one-subdivision recovers their theorem for even branch lengths.
item.dc:creator: Yuqi Zhao

item.title: Lonely Runner Relations
item.description: arXiv:2609.06259v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the \emph{Lonely Runner Conjecture} (LRC), conceived by J\"org M.~Wills in the 1960's: Given positive integers $n_1, n_2, \dots, n_k$, there exists a positive real number $t$ such that for all $1 \le j \le k$ the distance of $t \, n_j$ to the nearest integer is at least $\frac{ 1 }{ k+1 }$. We prove that for any counterexample or tight instance $\mathbf{n}$ of LRC, $\mathbf{m} \cdot \mathbf{n} = 0$ for some $\mathbf{m} \in \mathbb{Z}^k$ with $0 < \| \mathbf{m} \|_1 \le \min(2k+3, \ \frac{ k+1 }{ k-1 } \mathrm{flt}(k))$ where $\mathrm{flt}(k)$ denotes Khinchin's (1948) \emph{flatness constant} limiting the lattice width of a $k$-dimensional convex body without interior integer points. In other words, potential counterexamples to LRC lie on a finite set of hyperplanes in the parameter space. Our proofs use Fourier analysis and a geometric reformulation of LRC, and our results generalize to the situation of shifted lonely runners of varying measures of loneliness. Our results imply and generalize a theorem of Czerwi\'nski (2012) that when we choose $\mathbf{n}$ at random then, with probability tending to 1, the measure of loneliness $\frac{ 1 }{ k+1 }$ can be replaced by $\frac 1 2 - \epsilon$. We also show that the lattice width of the polyhedra appearing in conjunction with LRC grows linearly with the dimension.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Beck, Samuel Everett

item.title: Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank I: Amata-Crupi monomial modules, Kozlov polytopes, and r-vectors of simplicial complexes
item.description: arXiv:2609.23605v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $E$ be the exterior algebra on $n$ generators over a field, and let $F$ be a graded free $E$-module with $r$ generators, of degrees $d_1 \le \dots \le d_r$. We determine the convex hull of the set of Hilbert functions of the quotients $F/M$, where $M$ runs over the monomial submodules of Amata and Crupi. The hull is the Minkowski sum of $r$ shifted copies of one and the same simplex: the Kozlov simplex, which Kozlov proved in 1997 to be the convex hull of the $f$-vectors of simplicial complexes on $n$ vertices. For $r=1$ the statement is Kozlov's theorem, so this is a rank-$r$ generalization of it. We give a self-contained proof, including a proof of Kozlov's theorem from the local Lubell-Yamamoto-Meshalkin inequality, which is in essence Kozlov's own second proof, and the facet description of the Kozlov simplex that this proof contains. Along the way we isolate the class of submodules for which the argument works, the ideal-direct-sum modules, and show by example that the Hilbert function of a graded submodule outside that class need not be a shifted sum of $f$-vectors at all. The combinatorial content is stated separately, in language that uses no algebra, as a result on $r$-vectors of simplicial complexes and their $ff$-vectors. Finally we determine the vertices of the Minkowski sum at rank two: which sums of vertices of the summands survive as vertices. The facet descriptions at rank two, conjectured in the first version of this paper, and the vertex and facet descriptions at every rank are proved in Part IV of this series.
item.dc:creator: Jan Snellman

item.title: Log-concavity and Approximate Counting for Totally Unimodular Polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2609.39917v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a new lower bound on the number of lattice points of all totally unimodular polytopes, generalizing previous lower bounds on contingency tables, integer flows, and beyond. Our bound is based on the Gurvits capacity convex optimization problem, and thus our result implies an efficient deterministic algorithm for approximate counting of the lattice points up to an explicit exponential factor. We achieve our bounds by showing that the associated generating polynomials fit into a new general class of log-concave polynomials called VLC ("variable-wise log-concavity''). This also implies a conjecture of Ferroni and Higashitani on the evaluations of the Ehrhart polynomials of unimodular polytopes. The essential ingredient for these results is the resolution of Barvinok's log-concavity conjecture for contingency tables on lines, which was proven using ChatGPT 6 Astra. We conjecture a generalization of Barvinok's conjecture, which we believe will lead to stronger and more general bounds.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Leake, Maryam Mohammadi Yekta

item.title: The Choice Number of Random Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.35003v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1999, Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov conjectured that the choice number and chromatic number of the random graph $G(n,p)$ are asymptotically equal whenever $np\to\infty$. We prove their conjecture, showing that, with high probability, $$\mathrm{ch}(G(n,p))=(1+o(1))\chi(G(n,p))$$ whenever $np\to\infty$. This improves the bound $\mathrm{ch}(G(n,p))\le(2+o(1))\chi(G(n,p))$ for $np\to\infty$ and $p\le0.9$ obtained by Krivelevich and Vu in 2001. Our proof distinguishes two cases according to the size of independent sets. When independent sets of growing size are available, we establish a sharper uniform independent-set estimate that eliminates the factor-two loss in the bound of Krivelevich and Vu. When independent sets have bounded size, we establish a deterministic result showing that, under a suitable uniform independent-set condition, a proper colouring with bounded colour-class sizes yields an asymptotically matching upper bound on the choice number.
item.dc:creator: Lanchao Wang, Jiasheng Zeng

item.title: How many sorted projections determine any n points in k dimensions?
item.description: arXiv:2611.06470v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $d_1,\dots,d_m$ be directions in $\mathbb{R}^k$, where $k\ge 2$. A multiset $X$ of $n$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ projects to the $m$ multisets of numbers $\{\{x\cdot d_j : x\in X\}\}$, or equivalently to the $m$ sorted lists of these numbers. How many directions are needed for these projections to determine every multiset of $n$ points? Two simple bounds are known in every dimension: more than $(k-1)\log_2 n$ directions are always needed, and $(k-1)n+1$ directions in general position always suffice. In the plane much more is known: Matousek, Privetivy and Skovron showed that almost every choice of $O(\log n \log\log n)$ directions suffices. Whether anything similar holds in higher dimensions was left open by Dym, Wellershoff, Tsoukanis, Levy and Balan. We observe that two lemmas of Hair and Sahai, proved for list recovery of random linear codes, answer that question, and by tightening their argument we show that in every dimension almost every choice of $(4k-2)\ln(2n)\ln(k\log_2 2n)+k+1$ directions suffices. For $k\le 10$ this beats the linear bound once $n$ is larger than about 100: for example, 144 directions suffice for multisets of 1000 points in the plane, and an exact computation lowers this to 133. Letting some of the random blocks in their argument fail removes a factor $\log k$: almost every choice of $O(k\log n\log\log n)$ directions suffices, uniformly in $k$ and $n$. We also show that $2k-1$ directions never determine three points, so that the logarithmic lower bound is not tight; that every $m$ directions in the plane fail on some pair of multisets of size $O(1.65^m)$, improving the bound $O(1.80^m)$ of Matousek, Privetivy and Skovron; and that for each $k$, $m$ and $n$, either almost every choice of $m$ directions works or almost none does.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Gorham Lester, Raymond Hau S{\o}rensen

item.title: Uniquely balanced polyhedral complexes are highly connected
item.description: arXiv:2611.19866v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish higher connectivity of polyhedral complexes admitting a unique positive balanced top cycle. Our main result shows that, after quotienting by common lineality, every skeleton satisfies the corresponding higher connectivity property. The proof bounds the number of connected components surviving facet deletions by the dimension of the top-cycle space using homological and linear-algebraic arguments. As applications, we prove higher connectivity for all skeleta of arbitrary pointed polyhedral structures on tropical linear spaces of valuated matroids and Bergman fans including nonrealizable cases. These results answer questions raised by Maclagan and Yu.
item.dc:creator: Kisun Lee

item.title: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
item.description: arXiv:2611.20136v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The defect of a complex Hadamard matrix is the real dimension of the solution space obtained by linearizing the row orthogonality equations in the phases of the entries, with the first row and column fixed. It is known that defect zero implies isolation up to Hadamard equivalence. The converse, whether every isolated complex Hadamard matrix has defect zero, was open and is the square-matrix case of a conjecture of Banica, Ozteke and Pittau. We answer this question in the negative. We exhibit a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of order 13 with entries among the sixth roots of unity and show that it is isolated and has defect one. We prove isolation by showing that no nonzero solution of the linearized equations satisfies the second order condition obtained by the second author for directions of convergence of sequences of Hadamard matrices. In the language of commuting squares of matrix algebras, the example shows that an isolated commuting square can fail the span condition introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation.
item.dc:creator: Shannon Hall, Remus Nicoara

item.title: Polynomial bounds for quasiplanar graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.21416v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A graph $G$ is $k$-quasiplanar if it can be drawn in the plane without $k$ pairwise crossing edges. It was a longstanding conjecture that $n$-vertex $k$-quasiplanar graphs have $O_k(n)$ edges. Recently, using AI tools, we discovered that a theorem in topology proven by Beeker and Lazarovich essentially resolves this conjecture, with the implicit constant depending superexponentially on $k$. In this paper, we greatly improve this bound, showing that every $k$-quasiplanar $n$-vertex graph has at most $O(k^2n)$ edges. Our proof is purely combinatorial, based on a geometric charging scheme and Erd\H{o}s-Szekeres type arguments. We also construct $k$-quasiplanar graphs on $n$ vertices with $\Omega(k^{8/7}n)$, disproving the widely held belief that the right order of magnitude is $\Theta(kn)$.
item.dc:creator: Aleksa Milojevi\'c, Patryk Morawski, J\'anos Pach, Ankan Sadhu, Benny Sudakov, G\'abor Tardos, Istvan Tomon, Ji Zeng

item.title: A disproof of the van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk conjecture on the Davenport constant
item.description: arXiv:2611.24775v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Davenport constant $D(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence $S$ with terms from $G$ and with length $|S| \ge \ell$ has a nontrivial zero-sum subsequence. A long-standing conjecture, first proposed by van Emde Boas and Kruyswijk in 1969, states that $D(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1$ for all positive integers $n$ and $r$. We disprove this conjecture for every exponent $n=2k$ with $k\ge3$ odd. For each such $n$, we prove that $D(C_n^r)>r(n-1)+1$ for every $r\ge \frac{5n}{2}$. For rank $r=3$, we prove that the equality $D(C_n^3)=3n-2$ holds for all sufficiently large integers $n$.
item.dc:creator: Weidong Gao, Alfred Geroldinger, Guoqing Wang, Xiangneng Zeng

item.title: Combinatorial Dvoretzky Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.26253v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be an $n$-dimensional polytope such that $P \subset B_2^n$. Let $M^*(P)$ denote its mean width, and let $N$ be the number of facets (faces of dimension $n-1$) of $P$. We prove the following two bounds: (1) If $N \leq e^n$, then \[ M^*(P) \leq 1 - \frac{c}{\log^2(\frac{N}{n})}. \] (2) For arbitrary $N$, \[ M^*(P) \leq 1 - \frac{c}{n}N^{-\frac{2}{n-1}}. \] In both bounds, $c>0$ is an absolute constant.
item.dc:creator: Tomer Milo

item.title: Uniformly positive correlations in the dimer model and phase transition in lattice permutations on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d > 2$, via reflection positivity
item.description: arXiv:1909.06558v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Our first main result is that correlations between monomers in the dimer model in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ do not decay to zero when $d > 2$. This is the first rigorous result about correlations in the dimer model in dimensions greater than two and shows that the model behaves drastically differently than in two dimensions, in which case it is integrable and correlations are known to decay to zero polynomially. Such a result is implied by our more general, second main result, which states the occurrence of a phase transition in the model of lattice permutations, which is related to the quantum Bose gas. More precisely, we consider a self-avoiding walk interacting with lattice permutations and we prove that, in the regime of fully-packed loops, such a walk is `long' and the distance between its end-points grows linearly with the diameter of the box. These results follow from the derivation of a version of the infrared bound from a new general probabilistic settings, with coloured loops and walks interacting at sites and walks entering into the system from some `virtual' vertices. In dimension $d=3$ we use a transfer matrix argument to obtain a sharper infrared bound.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Taggi

item.title: Hilbert's Tenth problem and NP-completeness of Boolean Syllogistic with unordered cartesian product
item.description: arXiv:2101.00198v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We relate the decidability problem for BS with unordered cartesian product with Hilbert's Tenth problem and prove that BS with unordered cartesian product is NP-complete.
item.dc:creator: Domenico Cantone, Pietro Ursino

item.title: Elementary first-order model checking for sparse graphs
item.description: arXiv:2401.16230v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It is known that for subgraph-closed graph classes the first-order model checking problem is fixed-parameter tractable if and only if the class is nowhere dense [Grohe, Kreutzer, Siebertz, 2017]. However, the dependency on the formula size is non-elementary, and in fact, this is unavoidable even for the class of all trees [Frick and Grohe, 2004]. On the other hand, it is known that the dependency is elementary for classes of bounded degree [Frick and Grohe, 2004] as well as for classes of bounded pathwidth [Lampis, 2026]. In this paper we generalise these results and almost completely characterise subgraph-closed graph classes for which the model checking problem is fixed-parameter tractable with an elementary dependency on the formula size. Those are the graph classes for which there exists a number $d$ such that for every $r$, some tree of depth $d$ and size bounded by an elementary function of $r$ is avoided as an $(\le r)$-subdivision in all graphs in the class. In particular, this implies that if the class in question excludes a fixed tree as a topological minor, then first-order model checking for graphs in the class is fixed-parameter tractable with an elementary dependency on the formula size.
item.dc:creator: Jakub Gajarsk\'y, Micha{\l} Pilipczuk, Marek Soko{\l}owski, Giannos Stamoulis, Szymon Toru\'nczyk

item.title: Homotopy types of complexes of hyperplanes in quasi-median graphs and applications to right-angled Artin groups
item.description: arXiv:2503.08411v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we prove that, given two finite connected graphs $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$, if the two right-angled Artin groups $A(\Gamma_1)$ and $A(\Gamma_2)$ are quasi-isometric, then the infinite pointed sums $\bigvee_\mathbb{N} \Gamma_1^{\bowtie}$ and $\bigvee_\mathbb{N} \Gamma_2^{\bowtie}$ are homotopy equivalent, where $\Gamma_i^{\bowtie}$ denotes the simplicial complex whose vertex-set is $\Gamma_i$ and whose simplices are given by joins. These invariants are extracted from a study, of independent interest, of the homotopy types of several complexes of hyperplanes in quasi-median graphs (such as one-skeleta of CAT(0) cube complexes). For instance, given a quasi-median graph $X$, the \emph{crossing complex} $\mathrm{Cross}^\triangle(X)$ is the simplicial complex whose vertices are the hyperplanes (or $\theta$-classes) of $X$ and whose simplices are collections of pairwise transverse hyperplanes. When $X$ has no cut-vertex, we show that $\mathrm{Cross}^\triangle(X)$ is homotopy equivalent to the pointed sum of the links of all the vertices in the prism-completion $X^\square$ of $X$.
item.dc:creator: Carolyn Abbott, Anthony Genevois, Eduardo Martinez-Pedroza

item.title: Affine standard Lyndon words
item.description: arXiv:2505.15432v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this note, we establish the convexity and monotonicity for affine standard Lyndon words in all types, generalizing the $A$-type results of arXiv:2305.16299. We also derive partial results on the structure of imaginary standard Lyndon words and present a conjecture for their general form. Additionally, we provide computer code in Appendix that, in particular, allows to efficiently compute affine standard Lyndon words in exceptional types for all orders.
item.dc:creator: Corbet Elkins, Alexander Tsymbaliuk

item.title: A Higgs category for the cluster variety of triples of flags
item.description: arXiv:2509.04863v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The cluster variety of triples of flags (associated with a split simple Lie group of Dynkin type Delta) plays a key role in higher Teichmuller theory as developed by Fock-Goncharov, Jiarui Fei, Ian Le, ... and Goncharov-Shen. We refer to it as the basic triangle associated with Delta. In this paper, for simply laced Delta, we construct and study a Higgs category (in the sense of Yilin Wu) which we expect to categorify the basic triangle. This category is a certain exact dg category (in the sense of Xiaofa Chen) which is Frobenius and stably 2-Calabi-Yau. We show that it has indeed the expected cyclic group symmetry and that its derived category has the expected braid group symmetry. A key ingredient in our construction is a conjecture by Merlin Christ, whose proof occupies most of this paper. The proof is based on a new description of the Higgs category in terms of Gorenstein projective dg modules. Our techniques are in the spirit of Orlov in his work on triangulated categories of graded B-branes.
item.dc:creator: Bernhard Keller, Miantao Liu

item.title: Parke-Taylor Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2509.09323v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Parke--Taylor functions are certain rational functions on the Grassmannian of lines encoding MHV amplitudes in particle physics. For $n$ particles there are $n!$ Parke--Taylor functions, corresponding to all orderings of the particles. Linear relations between these functions have been extensively studied in the last years. We here describe all non-linear polynomial relations between these functions in a simple combinatorial way and study the variety parametrized by them, called the Parke--Taylor variety. We show that the Parke--Taylor variety is equal to the log canonical embedding of the moduli space $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ into $\mathbb{P}^{(n-2)!-1}$ due to Keel and Tevelev by exhibiting a concrete linear isomorphism with the realization in coordinates based on Kapranov's map. We also show that the intersection with the algebraic torus recovers the open part, $\mathcal{M}_{0,n}$. We give an explicit description of this isomorphism. Unlike the realization of the log canonical embedding by using the iterated Kapranov's map, this Parke--Taylor embedding very explicitly respects the symmetry of the $n$ marked points and is constructed in a single-step procedure, avoiding the intermediate embedding into a product of projective spaces.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Hollering, Dmitrii Pavlov

item.title: Learning Cut Distributions with Quantum Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2604.14381v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The probabilistic nature of quantum computation can be an asset rather than an obstacle for combinatorial optimization. In this work, we tackle the problem in which the sampled distribution itself is the object being optimized. This perspective is especially natural for fairness, coverage, and robustness objectives, where success is determined by the least-protected components rather than by average or best performance. We develop this idea by learning graph cut distributions. The resulting framework turns Fair Cut Cover into a native quantum distribution-learning problem and uses quantum circuits as trainable generators of cut distributions. We prove that standard QAOA at depth one achieves higher Fair Cut Cover values than optimal Semidefinite programming plus Gaussian hyperplane rounding on complete graphs with at least four vertices. We further establish a separation on a family of high-girth graphs using published QAOA evaluations, compare against a classical column-generation heuristic in numerical experiments, and examine finite-sampling and noise effects in quantum hardware implementations. These results suggest a broader role for this type of quantum algorithms: not merely finding good bitstrings, but learning useful combinatorial distributions for worst- and average-case-aware optimization.
item.dc:creator: Bao Bach, Cameron Ibrahim, Reuben Tate, Jad Salem, Stephan Eidenbenz, Ilya Safro

item.title: The Subtractive Divisor Orbit: Unconditional Bounds, Parity Constraints, and a Conditional Framework
item.description: arXiv:2604.25446v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $a(n)$ be the number of iterations of $F(m)=m-\tau(m)$ needed to reach zero, where $\tau(m)$ counts the positive divisors of $m$. Write $\Delta(n)=a(n)-a(n-1)$. We prove that for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $X$, each of the inequalities $\Delta(n)\ge X^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ and $\Delta(n)\le -X^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ holds for at least $X^{1-\varepsilon}$ integers $1\le n\le X$. The proof uses the identity $F(2m)=2F(m)$ at odd $m$ and the fact that an odd orbit first changes parity at a square. For every fixed $C>0$, a positive proportion of starting values $n\in(X,4X]$ satisfy $\left|a(n)-\frac{Cn}{\log n}\right|\gg_C\frac{\sqrt X}{\log X}$. For the hitting time itself we prove $a(x)\ll_b\frac{x}{(\log x)^b}$ for every $b<\log 2$, together with a lower bound having logarithmic exponent $2.988206\ldots$. On complete crossings of $(N,2N]$, with $Z=2N$, the logarithm of the step size has normal order $(\log 2)\log\log Z$, uniformly in the starting value. Computations through $10^9$ give the largest positive and negative first differences in this range.
item.dc:creator: Marco Mantovanelli

item.title: Rank Recursion for $q$-Whittaker and Macdonald Operators
item.description: arXiv:2606.12796v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce and prove a set of rank recurrence relations for $q$-Whittaker and Macdonald operators. We also derive an explicit expression for the $k$-th power of the $q$-Whittaker operators in terms of the $q$-deformed binomial probability distribution, and we express the rank recurrence relations for the Macdonald operators in terms of the Cauchy determinant.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Di Francesco, Hieu Trung Vu

item.title: A nine-line counterexample to a conjecture on the minimal degree of Jacobian relations
item.description: arXiv:2607.01985v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct two arrangements of nine lines in the complex projective plane with isomorphic intersection lattices, of weak combinatorics $(n_2,n_3,n_4)=(9,7,1)$, whose defining equations $f$ and $g$ satisfy $${\rm mdr}(f)=4,\qquad {\rm mdr}(g)=5.$$ Since $4<9/2$, this disproves a conjecture of the first author which would have implied Terao's Conjecture on the combinatorial nature of the freeness of line arrangements. Equivalently, the rank two vector bundle of logarithmic vector fields is strictly semistable for the first arrangement and stable for the second one. Hence the stability of this bundle is not determined by the intersection lattice, which gives a counterexample to a conjecture of Abe. The two arrangements also have different minimal free resolutions of their Milnor algebras. All computations are exact, and a short SINGULAR script performing them is included.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Dimca, Piotr Pokora

item.title: Power-saving density bounds for $K$-point configurations in $\mathbb{Z}^d$
item.description: arXiv:2609.13126v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $d,K,N\in \mathbb{N}$ with $K\geq 3$ and $d\geq 4K+4$. Let $\Delta\subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ be the vertex set of a nondegenerate $(K-1)$-simplex, and let $A\subseteq[N]^d$ contain no nontrivial similar copy of $\Delta$. We prove that \[ |A|\ll_{\Delta,d} N^{d-c_{\Delta,d}}, \] improving upon a polylogarithmic bound due to Magyar. We combine an induction-on-scale argument with the circle method, and we introduce a ``cut operator'' method to decouple the weighted exponential sum over the system of quadratic forms describing the simplex. Our proof combines ideas from graph theory, functional analysis, and the geometry of numbers. In the process, we apply Finner's fractional form of H\"older's inequality, the analytic large sieve, and Kim's mean value formula for primitive lattice flags.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Lott, \'Akos Magyar, Nagendar Reddy Ponagandla

item.title: Seed thresholds and degree variance in heterogeneous bootstrap percolation with growing degrees
item.description: arXiv:2610.04420v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study bootstrap percolation with independent vertex thresholds taking values one and two, with threshold-one probability $(1-c/d)/d$ for fixed $c>0$. The seed set is chosen uniformly among sets of a prescribed deterministic size, independently of the graph and thresholds. We prove threshold statements at fixed relative margins. For uniform simple graphs with prescribed nonnegative integer degrees of even sum and exact mean $d$, assume $\max_i|d_i-d|\le C\sqrt d$ and $c+1-v_n\ge\kappa>0$, where $v_n=\operatorname{Var}(D)/d$ and $C,\kappa$ are fixed. When $d\to\infty$ and $d=o(n^{1/7})$, the leading seed scale is $n(c+1-v_n)^2/(2d^4)$, without requiring a limit of $v_n$. At fixed relative margins below and above this scale, the final active set has size $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$, respectively, with high probability. For regular graphs, the supercritical conclusion strengthens to full activation. For $G(n,d/n)$, the same $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$ conclusions hold when $d\to\infty$ and $d^5/n\to0$, with seed scale $nc^2/(2d^4)$. Thus regular and independent-edge graphs have different coefficients at the same asymptotic mean degree. Local exploration estimates yield explicit inactive remainders and survive conditioning on simplicity in the prescribed model. We also quantify the precision obstruction to static inclusion transfer and compute deterministic response-barrier corrections, without identifying a shrinking random critical window. A separate appendix gives the corresponding fixed-margin terminal bounds for iid thresholds of fixed bounded support, with unchanged threshold-one probability and threshold-two mass bounded away from zero.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandr Rodionov

item.title: Polynomial complexity, random graphs, and strict ergodicity
item.description: arXiv:2611.08973v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct infinite words $w$ whose complexity functions are quadratically bounded, but whose discrete derivatives are not linearly bounded, resolving a question of Cassaigne. Moreover, we construct infinite words of polynomially bounded complexity, and subshifts of quasi-linear complexity, whose discrete derivatives do not decay compared to their complexity functions, thus exhibiting a typical exponentially-growing behavior. As an application, we give the first examples of subshifts of polynomial complexity whose Rauzy graphs do not have Benjamini-Schramm limits. Finally, we realize (up to an inevitable linear error factor) every function satisfying the necessary conditions, as the complexity function of a minimal, uniquely ergodic, cube-free subshift, strengthening previous realization results in this direction, and derive consequences for the growth of simple algebras and just-infinite semigroups satisfying nontrivial laws.
item.dc:creator: Be'eri Greenfeld, Paul-Henry Leemann, Carlos Gustavo Moreira, Efim Zelmanov

item.title: Congruence properties modulo powers of 3 for designated summands in partitions into odd parts
item.description: arXiv:2611.15164v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ into odd parts with designated summands. Using $3$-dissection identities and coefficient extraction, we obtain explicit polynomial expansions for the generating functions of two infinite families of arithmetic subsequences of $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$. We establish lower bounds for the $3$-adic valuations of the polynomial coefficients, thereby proving two infinite families of congruences conjectured by Lin (J. Number Theory,~2018). We then estimate the $3$-adic valuations of two-by-two determinants formed from consecutive coefficient vectors. These estimates yield two infinite families of internal congruences modulo high powers of $3$. The internal congruences and the initial generating functions also establish the generating-function congruences conjectured by Singh and Barman (Ramanujan J.,~2025).
item.dc:creator: Xingyi Li, Dazhao Tang

item.title: A Proof of Blackburn's Conjecture on Non-Overlapping Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.28776v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A code is non-overlapping if no nonempty proper prefix of a codeword is a suffix of a codeword. Let $S_n(q)$ be the largest size of a non-overlapping code of length $n$ over an alphabet of size $q$. Levenshtein proved that $S_n(q)\le c_nq^n$, where $c_n=(1/n)\bigl((n-1)/n\bigr)^{n-1}$. The codes $I^{n-1}J$, where $I$ and $J$ partition the alphabet, attain this bound when $n$ divides $q$, and Blackburn conjectured that for every $n$ and all sufficiently large $q$, the best such code is a maximum non-overlapping code. We prove this conjecture. The proof uses generating functions for the nested partitions that describe maximal non-overlapping codes. We also show that only the codes $I^{n-1}J$ with $|I|=(n-1)q/n$ and their reversals meet Levenshtein's bound.
item.dc:creator: Yeow Meng Chee
